subject: Iris-13B variant certification — pin vs fallback decision
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, John Diaz <john.diaz@novusai.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Iris-13B variant certification — pin vs fallback decision

Team,

We need a cross-functional decision on how we onboard the Iris-13B (v1.2) variant for Novus AI. Intake finished yesterday and the engineering/eval artifacts are attached (iris13b-eval-summary.pdf, compat-matrix.xlsx, canary-run-logs.txt). High-level callout: dev/eval found a small but repeatable tokenization drift on certain prompt shapes and quantization artifacts with 4-bit qparams on A100 L40 instances.

Options on the table (pick one, with caveats):
- Full pin (Novus gets a pinned serving version for GA) — requires us to guarantee compatibility and accept rollback slas.
- Limited pin (dedicated capacity only, telemetry gating + weekly regression checks).
- No pin (Iris offered as a fallback variant only; default model remains Helix-7B).

Asks:
1) Karthik/Evelyn: are the compat issues showstoppers for a pin? If not, what constraints do we need (HW types, quant profiles)?
2) Priya/Avery: contract/price implications if Novus requires a pinned SLA for Q4.
3) John (Novus): what is your tolerance for fallback/responses that may have small drift? Would limited pin suffice?

Please reply with your recommendation and rationale. My ask is to lock a direction by EOD Friday (2027-07-16) so legal/procurement can draft any necessary contract language.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Model Intake & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: iris13b-eval-summary.pdf (15 pages), compat-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), canary-run-logs.txt (text)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, John Diaz <john.diaz@novusai.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Iris-13B variant certification — pin vs fallback decision

Marissa — quick summary from infra/compat side. See compat-matrix.xlsx for test vectors.

TL;DR: I recommend Limited pin (dedicated capacity + telemetry gating) rather than a full unrestricted pin. Reasoning:
- Tokenization drift appears only when prompts include mixed-language tokens + long numeric sequences; we can mitigate with a prefix-normalizer at the routing layer, but that is a change to the request pipeline that needs QA.
- The quantization artifacts show up on some older Ampere kernels (A10G and certain driver combos). On A100 L40 and newer chips artifacts are negligible. We should constrain the pinned fleet to L40+ for Novus if they request deterministic output.
- Canary logs (attached) show 0.6% increase in hallucination signals on our safety eval hooks for the failing vectors — small but visible.

Operational ask if we go Limited pin:
- Add a telemetry gate that automatically disables Iris-13B for a customer if regression > 0.5% on the safety signal (owner: infra SRE).
- Initial canary duration: 7 days + nightly regression reports (owner: me).

Quoted for context:
> On Wed, 14 Jul 2027 at 09:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > We need a cross-functional decision on how we onboard the Iris-13B (v1.2) variant for Novus AI.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, John Diaz <john.diaz@novusai.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Iris-13B variant certification — pin vs fallback decision

Folks — procurement/legal here. A few points from the commercial perspective: 
- Novus's procurement request explicitly calls out a pinned model for the inference SLA clause (deterministic outputs for compliance). If we only provide a fallback variant, they will push for credits or a price concession.
- If we agree to a Limited pin tied to dedicated capacity, we should include an exception clause: pin is valid only on L40+ hardware and subject to regression-based auto-unpinning. Legal will want the exact regression thresholds and rollback timelines.
- We need confirmation from Novus on whether they can tolerate a temporary unpin/unavailable window in the event of an automatic rollback. If not, we may need to price a “managed pinned” offering with on-call SRE for immediate rollback support.

John — can you confirm whether Novus would accept a Limited pin with the following constraints?
1) Pinned fleet limited to L40+
2) Auto-unpin if regression > 0.5% (as Karthik suggested)
3) A 7-day canary before GA

If they cannot accept those constraints, we need to start a pricing/managed-support conversation.

Priya
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: John Diaz <john.diaz@novusai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nadia Rossi <nadia.rossi@edgeops.io>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Iris-13B variant certification — pin vs fallback decision

Thanks Marissa, team. Context from our side: several of our workflows are compliance-adjacent and we run deterministic checks against model outputs. Small drifts cause downstream re-ingestion and auditor flags. That said, we can accept a Limited pin with the constraints below as an interim solution: 
- Pinned fleet on L40+ only
- Telemetry gating and auto-unpin (we expect immediate notification and a 4-hour window to validate before contract-triggered penalties)
- 7-day canary + nightly regression reports; if regression persists beyond canary window, Novus reserves the right to require a rollback to Helix-7B with no penalty.

We can run a 4-week evaluation window (includes canary + extended monitoring). If telemetry and regression stay within the agreed thresholds, we will sign the pinned SLA for Q4.

John Diaz
Head of Product, Novus AI
john.diaz@novusai.com

Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Decision log: Iris-13B onboarding path for Novus AI

Decision summary (agreed): Limited pin for Novus AI under dedicated L40+ capacity, telemetry gating with auto-unpin at regression > 0.5%, 7-day canary then a 3-week extended monitor (total 4-week evaluation). If evaluation passes, draft pinned SLA for Q4.

Action items and owners:
- Karthik: implement telemetry gate and nightly regression report; run 7-day canary starting Monday 2027-07-19 (due: 2027-07-26). Attachments: canary-run-logs.txt (initial run saved).
- Evelyn/Avery: coordinate infra allocation for a dedicated L40+ pool and estimate burn-rate for pricing (due: 2027-07-20).
- Priya: prepare draft contract language for Limited pin (include auto-unpin clause and notification windows) and pricing delta (due: 2027-07-22).
- Marissa: own customer comms and high-level sign-off; schedule legal sync with Novus (meeting invite to follow).

Novus: John — thanks for quick clarity. Per your ask, we'll include a 4-hour validation window in the notification workflow before any contract penalties trigger; Priya will loop legal.

I'll drop the intake doc and the decision notes into INF-3212 and share the drive link. If anyone objects to the plan, raise it now — otherwise I'll move this to 'approved for Limited pin' and start the canary on 7/19.

Marissa
Head of Model Intake & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
